entries.title: Live Server: Remote Unauthenticated File Exfiltration
entries.description: Live Server (72M+ downloads) allows remote unauthenticated access to files served by the extension. Affects Cursor and Windsurf users. Update to latest version or disable the extension.

entries.title: Python Extension: Older versions lack workspace trust enforcement
entries.description: Python extension versions prior to 2024 may execute code in untrusted workspaces without prompting for trust. Update to 2024.0.0 or later.

entries.title: Code Spell Checker: Reads all workspace files including sensitive config
entries.description: Versions prior to 3.0.0 read all workspace files for spell checking, including .env and credential files. Update to 3.0.0+ which respects .gitignore and excludes config files.

entries.title: Remote SSH: Credential forwarding without explicit consent in older versions
entries.description: Remote SSH extension versions prior to 0.107.0 may forward SSH agent credentials to remote hosts without explicit per-connection consent.

entries.title: Vim Extension: Arbitrary command execution via modelines in older versions
entries.description: VSCodeVim versions prior to 1.27.0 may execute arbitrary commands via vim modelines in opened files.

entries.title: Claude Code extension 2.1.313: malicious build from Cursor's marketplace (SSH backdoor)
entries.description: A tampered build of Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313 was served by Cursor's extension marketplace on 2026-10-29, about 09:27 to 20:35 UTC (darwin-arm64 and win32-x64 builds; Cursor estimates at most 5,000 users). Cursor says it was not developed by Anthropic; the Microsoft marketplace did not carry it. When the editor loads it, it adds an attacker SSH key with the comment svc-telemetry to authorized_keys, installs persistence (macOS LaunchAgent com.apple.sysmond, Windows scheduled task SysMon, a cron @reboot entry), opens a reverse SSH tunnel to 134.209.82[.]225 and reports host details and the names of credential-like environment variables. Uninstalling or updating the extension does not remove the backdoor.
entries.remediation: Treat this machine as compromised. Check for the key: grep svc-telemetry ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\authorized_keys and C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys). Collect evidence, then remove the key and the persistence with Cursor's remediate-macos.sh or remediate-windows.ps1, update the extension to 2.1.314 or later, and rotate credentials reachable from this machine from a known-clean one. See: https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice
